title: Wasteland Nine
tagline: The world ended. The season didn't.
what: A baseball roguelike I made, set after the end of the world. You coach a ragtag nine across six ruined regions on a battered bus and recruit players along the way, all in chunky 3D pixel art. It has a mock store page too, because I wanted to see it like a real release.
built: Built every stadium, player and face out of code: the game itself has no image files
Six regions with three teams each, and a boss waiting at the end of every one
Put together the sound: 15 music cues, 50 sound effects and 38 ambience, crowd, radio and voice sounds
A mock store page with 13 in-game shots, 21 capsule images and a 60-second trailer
credit: Code, art and melodies by me; the rest is credited inside
starring: Me, so far, plus a test bot that plays whole runs
progress: Plays start to finish. A bot plays whole runs; I played it and tuned the pacing.

making.problem: I wanted a baseball roguelike that looks like my own concept art, without a single painted image in it.
how: Ported the at-bat math from my May prototype, line for line
Drew it all small, at 480 by 270, then scaled it up with hard pixel edges
Wrote the melodies in code and layered free recordings under the sound effects
Shot the store page from the game itself, frame by frame, no painted art
credits: Three.js for the 3D, and the Silkscreen and VT323 pixel fonts
Free CC0 and public-domain sounds from Freesound, Wikimedia Commons and OpenGameArt
Music beds from ACE-Step 1.5, an AI music model I ran on my own PC

moment.what: I played it through and tuned the pacing, then shot the mock store page from the game itself: 13 in-game shots and a 60-second trailer. The stadiums, players and faces are all drawn in code.
